decisions.reason: It builds directly on the firm's core geospatial integration know-how, is supported by in-house R&D, and its own product page suggests enough commitment and interpretability for further improvement.

A building data digital twin service extends the firm's established geospatial and enterprise-integration capabilities, so management is likely to retain it and learn from early market feedback rather than withdraw it quickly.

Although authentication is a somewhat more technical adjacency than classic GIS functions, it is still close enough to the firm's solution stack and R&D base that the firm would more likely refine it than drop it.

An open GIS application development framework fits very closely with the firm's long-standing software-component, consulting, and standards-oriented capabilities, making continued commercialization likely.

This identity and access service is clearly positioned for GIS applications and enterprise integration, so despite some adjacency it remains close to the firm's knowledge base and is likely to be kept for further development.
